lines.trans: The new felt bushing is dry and the brass pin sits tight, madam.
Your hands are as steady as a watchmaker's, Tariq. May I try the key?
Go right ahead—gently first, then full weight.
Listen... D! Clear, round, and zero rattle in the wood!
Sounds a tiny bit flat next to the note above it, doesn't it?
You have a good ear, Tariq! Turn the steel tuning wrench a hair to the right.
Right here... tell me when to stop.
Right... there! Hold it! Play a warm G-major chord with me—listen!
Look at that—this old walnut box fills the whole glass room!
Wait until you hear Mazen's aunt's finished waltz tomorrow afternoon, Tariq.
Let me screw the front panel back on and polish the brass pedals.
Thank you, Tariq. After thirty quiet years, this piano has its voice back.

meanings.note: Standard/polite word for 'ear' alongside colloquial ذان; feminine in agreement.

examples.text: قرب أذنك واسمع رنة الوتر الصافية.
examples.trans: Bring your ear close and listen to the clear ring of the string.

examples.text: مدام سعاد عندها أذن موسيقية ما بتخطئ نغمة.
examples.trans: Madam Suad has a musical ear that never misses a note.

meanings.note: Relational adjective from أمام ('in front of'): الغرفة الأمامية / الباب الأمامي.

examples.text: علقنا اللوحة الجديدة جنب البوابة الأمامية.
examples.trans: We hung the new sign beside the front gate.
The front windows look straight out onto the lane.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite noun أول means 'first' (أول يوم 'first day'); after a definite noun الأول / الأولى agrees in gender (الصفحة الأولى 'the first page'). Also used adverbially ('first').

examples.trans: Welcome on your first day of work!
Read the first page calmly.

meanings.note: Warm spoken Levantine affirmation ('yes! / exactly!').

examples.text: أيوا، هاد هو اللحن اللي كنت أدور عليه!
examples.trans: Yes, that's the exact melody I was looking for!

examples.text: أيوا بالزبط، حط الكراسي جنب القوس.
examples.trans: Yes, right there—put the chairs beside the arch.

meanings.note: Everyday noun for a finger or toe; dual إصبعين ('two fingers'), broken plural أصابع.

examples.trans: Pull the paper out gently with two fingers.

examples.text: خلي أصابعك بعيدة عن الفرن السخن.
examples.trans: Keep your fingers away from the hot oven.

meanings.note: Appears in everyday speech inside warm set phrases such as إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again!').

examples.trans: See you soon, sir!
Goodbye and until next time.

meanings.note: Parts of the body in pairs are feminine in Arabic; 'my hands' is إيديي (iideyyi).

examples.trans: He washed his hands with warm water.
I planted the flowers with my own hand.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine question word for 'when?' (alongside متى).

examples.text: إيمتى رح نعلق الشيش الأخضر عالشبابيك؟
examples.trans: When are we going to hang the green shutters on the windows?

examples.text: إيمتى بيجهز أول فوج خبز الصبح؟
examples.trans: When does the first batch of bread come out in the morning?

meanings.note: Command to a male to wait.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
The suitcase is still waiting for its owner.

meanings.note: The universal relative pronoun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.trans: That is what I want.
The inn that keeps a stranger's bag safe.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word (from Turkish burgu) for a metal screw.

examples.trans: I tightened the screw with the small screwdriver.
The chair needs a new screw.

meanings.note: Means 'after' (بعد المطر) and with a future span 'in' (بعد أربعين دقيقة 'in forty minutes').

examples.trans: He arrives in forty minutes.
How lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'then, next, afterwards' (وبعدين 'and then').

examples.trans: Lift the handle first, and then push.
Have some tea and then we will talk.

meanings.note: Everyday word for 'tomorrow' (بكرا الصبح 'tomorrow morning').

examples.text: بكرا الصبح رح نسبق المي الباردة!
examples.trans: Tomorrow morning we will beat the cold water!
We booked a quiet dinner — will you join us tomorrow?

meanings.note: The musical instrument.

examples.trans: The sound of the piano is warm and calm.
I learned piano when I was young.

تفضّل.gloss: to please come in / sit / go ahead / here you are

meanings.en: to please come in / sit / go ahead / here you are
meanings.note: Essential Jordanian hospitality verb used mostly in the imperative: تفضل (to a man), تفضلي (to a woman), تفضلوا (plural).

examples.trans: Please have a seat, ma'am!
Here you go, hot mint tea.

meanings.note: The number 30.

examples.trans: They have given us thirty days in the letter.
The bill is thirty-eight dinars.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ثابتة, plural: ثابتين).

examples.trans: Hold the torch steady on the pipe.
The flame's color is steady blue.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بثبت, بيثبت).

examples.trans: Hold still a moment and listen to that sound!

examples.text: الكرسي ثبت بعد ما شدينا البرغي.
examples.trans: The chair held firm once we tightened the screw.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: جديدة, plural: جداد).

examples.trans: I am Nour, the new receptionist.
I installed a new lightbulb last week.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بجرب, بيجرب).

examples.trans: This sweater is clean and new — try it on.
We tried the new recipe and it turned out delicious.

meanings.note: Craftsman's term for a small protective felt, rubber, or leather ring/bushing inside hardware or instruments.

examples.text: غيرنا جلدة اللباد الصغيرة تحت المفتاح فاختفت الطقة.
examples.trans: We replaced the tiny felt bushing under the key and the click vanished.

examples.text: شديت الصامولة بعد ما ركبت جلدة جديدة.
examples.trans: I tightened the nut after fitting a new washer.

meanings.note: Commonly used preposition for indicating proximity, next to, or beside.

examples.trans: Put a napkin beside every cup.
There is no light beside the bed.

meanings.note: Collective noun for walnuts; خشب جوز is walnut wood. (Not to be confused with جوز 'husband; pair', a different everyday sense.)

examples.trans: I bought a kilo of walnuts at the market.
The cake has walnuts and honey in it.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to speak, talk, tell' (بحكي / حكى).

examples.trans: Salma chats with all the neighbours.
Tell me everything I need to know.

meanings.note: Used for the material wood or timber.

examples.trans: The wooden ceiling is warm and quiet.
This is a hand-carved wooden train.

meanings.note: Very frequent Jordanian verb: خليني ('let me'), خلينا ('let us'), خليك ('stay!'), خلي ('keep/leave').

examples.trans: Let us open the door together.
Hot bread makes people pleasant!

meanings.note: Used to describe warm weather, warm water, or a cozy feeling.

examples.trans: The bread is warm and fresh from the oven.
Sitting in the attic is cozy when it rains.

meanings.note: Instrumental noun from داس ('step/press with the foot'); names piano pedals or car/bicycle pedals.

examples.text: لمعت دواسات البيانو النحاس حتى صارت تبرق.
examples.trans: I polished the brass piano pedals until they gleamed.

examples.text: اضغطي عالدواسة اليمين بنعومة بآخر المقطع.
examples.trans: Press the right pedal gently at the end of the passage.

meanings.note: Levantine musical term (from Ottoman/Persian dūzān) for tuning stringed instruments; مفتاح دوزان is a tuning wrench.

examples.text: البيانو القديم حافظ على دوزانه بشكل مدهش.
examples.trans: The old piano held its tuning remarkably well.

examples.text: لقينا مفتاح الدوزان بالدرج التحتاني للصندوق.
examples.trans: We found the tuning key in the bottom drawer of the chest.

رجع.gloss: to return; come back; start again

meanings.en: to return; come back; start again
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (برجع, بيرجع).

examples.trans: Can you run there and come back in ten minutes?
Did the pipe start dripping again?

ركب.gloss: to ride; take (a bus); fit cleanly

meanings.en: to ride; take (a bus); fit cleanly
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بركب, بيركب).

examples.trans: We rode the same morning bus!
The new brass thread fitted cleanly.

meanings.note: Solfege name standard in Arabic music education for the note D (ري الوسطى 'middle D').

examples.text: نغمة ري الوسطى هي المفتاح اللي كان ساكت.
examples.trans: Middle D is the exact key that was silent.

examples.text: الأغنية بتنزل بهدوء على نغمة ري بالأخير.
examples.trans: The song settles gently onto D near the end.

meanings.note: Used almost universally in the Levantine adverbial phrase بالزبط (biz-zabt, 'exactly / right on').

examples.text: هاد هو اللون الأخضر اللي بدنا إياه بالزبط!
examples.trans: That is the exact shade of green we want!

examples.text: وصل السايق عالباب الساعة تنتين بالزبط.
examples.trans: The driver arrived at the gate at two o'clock sharp.

meanings.note: Extremely common Levantine preposition meaning 'like' or 'similar to'.

examples.trans: I want a glass of tea like yesterday.
Do it the way I taught you.

meanings.note: Traditional Levantine craft title formed from ساعة ('watch/clock') + occupational suffix ـاتي.

examples.text: استعرت مفتاح صغير من جارنا الساعاتي بالحارة.
examples.trans: I borrowed a tiny wrench from our watchmaker neighbour down the lane.
A watchmaker trains his hand for precision and patience.

meanings.note: Respectful and warm Levantine title for a woman ('Madam / Mrs. / lady').

examples.text: يسلموا إيديكي يا ست سعاد عاللحن الحلو.
examples.trans: Bless your hands, Madam Suad, for the lovely melody.

examples.text: كل ست وشيخ بالحارة معزومين عالافتتاح.
examples.trans: Every lady and elder on the lane is invited to the opening.

meanings.note: Means peace, safety, and is widely used as a greeting or farewell.

examples.text: يا سلام عالشمس الدافية بعد المطر!
examples.trans: Oh how lovely, warm sun after the rain!
They live in safety and peace in the neighbourhood.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بسمع, بيسمع).

examples.trans: Did you hear the gate bell downstairs?
Inside the courtyard we hear the tree leaves.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a year.

examples.trans: The building is eighty years old.
I have not seen him for three years.

meanings.note: Singulative of شعر ('hair'); used idiomatically for tiny precision ('by a hair').

examples.text: شديت الوتر شعرة خفيفة فرجعت النغمة بمحلها.
examples.trans: I tightened the string by a hair and the note clicked into place.

examples.text: اللوحة مستقيمة مية بالمية، مش مايلة ولا شعرة.
examples.trans: The sign is a hundred percent level—not tilted by a single hair.

meanings.note: Describes a pure musical note, clear sky (سما صافية), or clear broth.

examples.text: نغمة البيانو طلعت صافية متل المي.
examples.trans: The piano note rang out crystal clear.

examples.text: انشالله تضل السما صافية طول نهار التنين.
examples.trans: Hopefully the sky stays clear all day Monday.

meanings.note: Everyday word confirming something is right ('right! / true!').

examples.text: صح! في صفحة تانية ورا الرسالة.
examples.trans: Right! There is a second page behind the letter.
What you say is completely true.

meanings.note: Adjective used for size (small) or age (young), masculine singular.

examples.trans: We found a little wooden train in the bag.
There are two small streets on the left.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: صناديق.

examples.trans: The screwdriver is inside the toolbox.
We moved four boxes out of the hallway.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أصوات.

examples.trans: I heard the sound of rain on the window.
His voice is calm and polite on the phone.

meanings.note: Arabic/French solfège name for the note G (دو، ري، مي، فا، صول، لا، سي).

examples.text: كورد صول الكبير طلع صافي ودافي بالغرفة.
examples.trans: The G major chord rang out clear and warm in the room.

examples.text: نغمة صول صارت متوازنة تماما مع باقي الأوتار.
examples.trans: The G note is now balanced perfectly with the other strings.

meanings.note: Instance noun (اسم مرة) from onomatopoeic طق ('pop, click').

examples.text: سمعنا طقة خفيفة لما فتح القفل النحاس.
examples.trans: We heard a soft click when the brass lock opened.

examples.text: اشتغلت اللمبة بهدوء بدون ولا طقة.
examples.trans: The lamp came on quietly without a single pop.

meanings.note: Pronounced duhur in everyday Jordanian: الظهر means 'at noon / midday'.

examples.trans: He will arrive Friday at noon.
The sun is high at midday.

meanings.note: Form II Jordanian verb for filling buckets, cups, or rooms with light.

examples.trans: We filled the two buckets with warm soapy water.
Morning sunlight fills the room with brightness.

meanings.note: Appreciative Levantine adjective for fine aged wood, stonework, or heritage objects.

examples.text: خشب الجوز العتيق بالبيانو صوته دافي وأصيل.
examples.trans: The vintage walnut wood in the piano has a warm, resonant tone.

examples.text: الباب العتيق رجع جديد بعد الصنفرة والدهان.
examples.trans: The old heritage door looked new again after sanding and painting.

meanings.note: Arabic distinguishes father's sister (عمة, feminine of عمّ) from mother's sister (خالة).

examples.text: عمتي كانت تعزف عالبيانو كل يوم جمعة.
examples.trans: My paternal aunt used to play the piano every Friday.

examples.text: هاد الدفتر الأخضر هدية من عمتي.
examples.trans: This green notebook is a gift from my aunt.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعزف, بيعزف).

examples.trans: I am still waiting for you to play the scale!

examples.text: الكبير كان يعزف بيانو كل جمعة.
examples.trans: The older boy used to play piano every Friday.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for a room in a house or building.

examples.trans: We have eight comfortable rooms at the guesthouse.
Room four is ready and clean.

meanings.note: Musical loanword (from French valse) for a triple-time piano or orchestral waltz.

examples.text: عزفت سعاد فالس هادي بغرفة القزاز.
examples.trans: Suad played a gentle waltz in the sunroom.

examples.text: عنوان الورقة القديمة هو فالس الساحة.
examples.trans: The title on the old sheet is Courtyard Waltz.

meanings.note: Used as a preposition or adverb meaning 'above', 'over', or 'upstairs'.

examples.trans: The window is above the old tree.
Let us go upstairs to see the room.

meanings.note: Tempered steel used for piano strings and tools.

examples.text: أوتار البيانو مصنوعة من سلك فولاذ قوي.
examples.trans: Piano strings are made of strong steel wire.

examples.text: هاد المفك راسه فولاذ وما بينحني.
examples.trans: This screwdriver has a steel tip and never bends.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقدر, بيقدر).

examples.text: بنقدر نقدم زبدة مالحة مع المربى؟
examples.trans: Can we serve salted butter with jam?

examples.text: ليش ما قدرت تعطيه القطار بإيدك؟
examples.trans: Why could you not hand him the train yourself?

meanings.note: Refers to the material glass, a pane of glass, or sometimes a glass bottle.

examples.trans: Look at the courtyard through the window glass.
We wiped the glass this morning until it shone.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: كاملة, plural: كاملين).

examples.trans: He hired her for a full-time job at the guesthouse.
They stayed with us a full week.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: كبيرة, plural: كبار).

examples.trans: We use this big paper ledger.
You know older brothers well!

meanings.note: A highly versatile quantifier used to mean 'all of', 'every', or 'the whole'.

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everyone is happy in the courtyard today.

meanings.note: Everyday musicians' term in Amman for a piano or guitar chord.

examples.text: اعزفي كورد صول الكبير واسمعي كيف رنته صافية.
examples.trans: Play a G major chord and hear how clear it rings.

examples.text: ختمت سعاد الأغنية بكورد هادي وطويل.
examples.trans: Suad ended the song with a quiet, lingering chord.

meanings.note: Dense wool felt that cushions piano hammers and bushings.

examples.text: لباد الصوف بيخلي صوت البيانو ناعم ودافي.
examples.trans: Wool felt keeps the piano's tone soft and warm.

examples.text: حطينا قطع لباد صغيرة تحت رجلين الكراسي.
examples.trans: We stuck small felt pads under the chair legs.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بلف, بيلف).

examples.text: لفي شمال برا البوابة وامشي دغري.
examples.trans: Turn left outside the gate and walk straight.
Turn left at the stair landing.

meanings.note: Core word in إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again / goodbye!') and also 'reunion / meeting'.

examples.trans: Goodbye, have a pleasant trip!

examples.text: كان لقاء دافي بعد غياب طويل.
examples.trans: It was a warm reunion after a long absence.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بلمع, بيلمع).

examples.trans: Are you polishing the lanterns for noon?

examples.text: خمستعشر سنة وأنا بلمع مفاتيح النحاس!
examples.trans: Fifteen years I have been polishing the brass keys!

meanings.note: Refers to a whiteboard (اللوح الأبيض), wooden plank, or windowpane (لوح قزاز).

examples.text: كتبنا مهام الأسبوع التلاتة عاللوح الأبيض.
examples.trans: We wrote the three tasks for the week on the whiteboard.

examples.text: نضفنا كل ألواح القزاز من الغبرة القديمة.
examples.trans: We cleaned all the glass panes of their old dust.

meanings.note: Used to describe something securely fastened, well-constructed, or sealed tightly.

examples.text: غطا المرتبان محكم عشان ما تدخل الرطوبة عالسكر.
examples.trans: The jar lid is tight-fitting so dampness doesn't get into the sugar.

examples.text: تأكدنا إن إطار الشباك محكم قبل مطر الليل.
examples.trans: We made sure the window frame was snug before the night rain.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مدورة, plural: مدورين).

examples.trans: Where should I hang the round mirror?
We put a round wooden table in the corner.

meanings.note: General word for a metal nail, peg, or tuning pin inside a piano.

examples.text: ركبت المفتاح بحذر على مسمار الدوزان التاني.
examples.trans: I fitted the wrench carefully onto the second tuning pin.

examples.text: دقينا مسمارين صغار عشان نعلق لوحة البوابة.
examples.trans: We tapped in two small nails to hang the gate sign.

meanings.note: Means both a door key and a mechanic's spanner/wrench (مفتاح حديد iron wrench).

examples.trans: Here is the key to room four.
We have eight brass keys on the board.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: موسيقية, plural: موسيقيين).

examples.trans: Play the musical scale slowly.
She has a sensitive musical ear.

meanings.note: Vivid Levantine word for a tiny pinch or scrap; ولا نتفة means 'not a single scrap / zero'.

examples.text: ما ضل ولا نتفة غبرة عالرفوف.
examples.trans: Not a single speck of dust is left on the shelves.

examples.text: حطي نتفة قرفة صغيرة فوق الكيك.
examples.trans: Put a tiny pinch of cinnamon on top of the cake.

meanings.note: Used for the metal or objects made of it.

examples.trans: We polished the brass keys in the morning.
The brass pot is old and engraved.

meanings.note: Form I intransitive verb (nishif / byinshaf) meaning 'dry out'.

examples.text: لما تطلع الشمس، الحجار بتنشف بسرعة.
examples.trans: When the sun comes out, the stones dry quickly.

examples.text: استنينا ساعتين لحد ما ينشف الدهان.
examples.trans: We waited two hours until the paint dried.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: نغمات.

examples.text: سمع كل نغمة من البيانو بهدوء.
examples.trans: He listened quietly to every note of the piano.
The chime of the bell is gentle, not harsh.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنزل, بينزل).

examples.trans: The guests will come down at half past seven.
I came down to ask about the sink water.

meanings.note: Used chiefly in the idiomatic Levantine adverbial phrase عالهدا ('gently, slowly, carefully').

examples.text: حركي أصابع رجلك عالهدا وخدي نفس عميق.
examples.trans: Wiggle your toes gently and take a deep breath.

examples.text: نزلنا السلم عالهدا خطوة خطوة بالساحة.
examples.trans: We brought the ladder down gently step by step in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The morning quiet of the courtyard is very peaceful.
We talked the matter through calmly and patiently.

meanings.note: Standard adverb for physical location.

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
Stay right here a minute.

meanings.note: Used for physical weight on a foot, scale measurements, or poetic meter.

examples.text: لا تحطي أي وزن عكاحلك اليوم أبدا.
examples.trans: Don't put any weight on your ankle at all today.

examples.text: قيس وزن الطحين والسكر بالميزان قبل العجن.
examples.trans: Weigh the flour and sugar on the scale before kneading.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بوقف, بيوقف).

examples.trans: A yellow taxi stopped outside the gate!
My heart stopped at page one!

meanings.note: Used in negative constructions or as a strong negative emphasis.

examples.trans: Is the window facing the street or the courtyard?
Not a single drop of water on the table!

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Warm Jordanian/Levantine thank-you when someone hands you food, tea, or help (short for يسلموا إيديك 'may your hands be blessed').

examples.trans: Thank you, Salma, for the hot tea!
Thank you, it smells wonderful!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The green pharmacy is on your right.
We hung the board to the right of the desk.
